items.lawCode: Add §6507-a Ed L; amd §97-nnn, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4200

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the education law and the state finance law, in
relation to stabilizing the office of the professions account


 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to stabilize the Office of the Professions
Account (OP Account) by imposing a 15% surcharge on individual
registration and re-registration fees for the professions overseen by
the State Education Department's Office of the Professions, with the
exception of fees dedicated for deposit to the Professional Medical
Conduct Account. The OP Account, which provides the entire funding
source for the Office of the Professions, can no longer effectively
sustain the fiscal viability of the Office despite strict fiscal
controls and dramatic reductions in operational expenses.

This bill is necessary to continue the effective and efficient
operation of the Office of the Professions in meeting its annual
responsibilities, including issuing approximately 50,000 professional
licenses, processing more than 250,000 registrations, overseeing
continuing education of licensed professionals, investigating and
resolving over 7,000 professional misconduct complaints annually,
reviewing 300 educational programs, conducting 15,000 individual
reviews of non-traditional education, responding to one million calls
and emails on licensure and practice issues, providing professional
practice guidance, and monitoring 300 individuals in the Professional
Assistance Program.

 SUMMARY OF THE PROVISIONS OF THE BILL :

Section 1 would add §6507-a to the Education Law to authorize the
Commissioner of Education to impose a 15% surcharge, rounded upward to
the nearest dollar, on any professional registration fee imposed on a
profession pursuant to Title 8 of the Education Law.

Section 2 would amend subdivision 2 of §97-nnn of the State Finance
Law to clarify that surcharges established by statute, such as the
surcharge that would be established by section 1 of this act, are
subject to deposit in the OP Account.

Section 3 is the effective date.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT OF THE BILL :

The Department's Office of the Professions currently licenses 48
professions. The OP Account was created by Chapter 436 of the Laws of
1997 to collect fees charged for the Office of the Professions'
administration and regulation of the professions, which included fees
for professional registration, licensing, continuing education, and
limited permits. Currently, fees for registration range from $30 to
$210, with the majority of existing fees falling into the categories
of $50, $155 or $210. These registration fees have not been raised
since 1989, with the exception of the registration fee for physicians,
which was increased in 1996. While the number of professions,
licensees, and mandated oversight responsibilities continue to grow
(for instance, there has been a 25% increase in the number of
professions since 1997), revenues have not kept pace with inflation
and are not adequate to accommodate newly required responsibilities.
As such, this revenue account, which provides the entire funding
source for the Office of the Professions, can no longer effectively
sustain the fiscal viability of the Office, and a modest fee increase

is necessary to continue the effective and efficient operation of the
Office.

This bill will raise the additional revenue necessary to stabilize the
Office of the Professions through the imposition of a surcharge on all
registration fees imposed on licensed professionals providing
professional services, with the exception of fees dedicated for
deposit to the Professional Medical Conduct Account. It will only
impose minimal financial impact on individual licensees.
Specifically, each licensee would be required to pay an additional 15%
surcharge on each fee required for professional registration. The
majority of the increases for triennial registration fees would be $8,
$24 or $32.

It is projected that this bill will provide an additional $4 Million
in revenue to the OP Account for the continued efficient operation of
the Office of the Professions. The Office of the Professions serves a
very important role in regulating 48 professions and in doing so,
helps ensure the proper preparation, quality of performance, and
continued development of these licensed professionals. Moreover, the
Office ensures the public's protection from professional misconduct
and the unauthorized practice of a profession. The Office also ensures
the quality of professional education programs. The critical work of
the Office of the Professions contributes to the well-being.
stability, and economic health of New York State.

Without this fee increase, investigations of professional misconduct
and unauthorized practice of a profession will be seriously undermined
and patients and clients may be harmed.  Increased funding of the OP
Account is necessary to protect the public from individuals who
fraudulently represent themselves as licensees.  This fee increase is
not only necessary to protect the public from these unlicensed,
untrained individuals, but also to preserve the public's confidence in
the professions when seeking and obtaining services from licensed
health, design, and business professionals.

Further, without this fee increase, evaluations of professional
education programs will likely be delayed, harming both schools and
students. Necessary information may not be provided to the public,
hospitals, professionals, the legislature, and many other
stakeholders.  Productivity across all of the Office of the
Professions would be adversely affected, leading to the frustration of
licensees, applicants, employers and the public. Therefore, this bill
is necessary to preserve the quality of such educational programs and
to promote effective communication with the public, licensees and
other such constituencies.

 BUDGETARY IMPLICATIONS OF THE BILL :

This bill will not impose any additional costs on the State. We
estimate that this bill will generate approximately $4 Million
annually in additional revenues for the OP Account. This bill is
necessary for the effective and efficient operation of the
Department's Office of the Professions, which includes the
registration and licensing of 48 professions, the continuing education
of such licensed professionals, the investigation and prosecution of
professional misconduct, and other related functions of such Office.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new bill.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill would take effect immediately, provided that section 1 of
the bill, which imposes the surcharge, would take effect 30 days after
it becomes a law and would apply to fees received by the Department on
or after such date.

summary: Authorizes the commissioner of education to impose a 15% surcharge on any professional fee imposed pursuant to title 8 of the education law that is subject to deposit in the office of professions account.
